hook: The rich young man who gave everything away and preached to the birds.

pages.x: Francesco Bernardone was born in Assisi in 1181, the son of a rich cloth merchant. He loved fine clothes, parties and songs, and dreamed of becoming a knight. In a war with nearby Perugia he was captured and spent a year in a prison cell.

Praying in the ruined chapel of San Damiano, he heard Christ say: "Francis, repair my church." He sold his father's cloth to pay for it. His furious father dragged him before the bishop, and Francis took off all his clothes, handed them back, and said he now had only one father, in heaven.

He lived as a beggar, cared for lepers and preached in the streets. Followers joined him, owning nothing, and in 1209 the pope approved his order, the Franciscans, the "little brothers". With Clare of Assisi he founded an order for women, the Poor Clares.

Francis called all creatures his brothers and sisters. The stories say he preached to a flock of birds, which stayed to listen, and tamed a wolf that was terrorising the town of Gubbio, making the townspeople promise to feed it.

In 1219, during a Crusade in Egypt, he crossed the battle lines to meet Sultan al-Kamil, hoping to convert him or die a martyr. The sultan listened politely and sent him back unharmed. Francis came home with a new respect for Muslim prayer.

At Christmas 1223, in the village of Greccio, he set up a manger in a cave with a live ox and donkey, so people could see how poor the baby Jesus had been. It was the first Christmas crib, now set up in homes and churches around the world.

Almost blind, he wrote one of the first great poems in Italian, praising God for "Brother Sun", "Sister Moon", "Brother Wind" and even "Sister Death". He died in 1226, lying on the bare ground, and was made a saint only two years later.
Francis is one of the best-loved saints. His order spread around the world, he is the patron saint of animals and the environment, and in 2013 a new pope took his name.
pts: Patron saint of animals and the environment
